name: Ratio Diagonal Spread (Front Ratio Diagonal)
summary: Sell two shorter-dated options at one strike against one longer-dated option at a different strike; a diagonal financed into a credit at the cost of one uncovered short.
max_profit: At the short strike at front expiry: the intrinsic gain on the long from the long strike up to the short strike, plus the net credit.
max_loss: UNDEFINED above the short strike - the second short call is uncovered. Each dollar above the short strike costs $100 net per unit once the first short is offset by the long.
breakevens: Downside: the long strike plus or minus the net credit. Upside: approximately short strike + (max profit at the short strike)/100.

greeks.delta: positive below the short strike, turning negative above it
greeks.gamma: negative above the short strike, and it accelerates

when_to_use: A moderately bullish view with a hard ceiling - you expect the underlying to rise to but not through the short strike. Included for completeness; the naked leg makes it level 4 and it is not appropriate for a $50k account. The level-3-legal way to express the same view is a bull call diagonal plus a separately covered short call spread.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4 - one of the two short calls has no covering long. The automation must reject this at level 3.
Long leg 60-120 DTE at delta 0.50-0.70; shorts 21-45 DTE at delta 0.20-0.30, strike above the long strike.
Short expiry strictly before the long expiry.
Net credit >= $0; never pay a debit for a structure with an uncovered leg.
Short strike must sit above a durable technical resistance level and beyond 1.5 x the front-month expected move.
Size on full naked margin for the uncovered contract.
management_rules: Stop if the underlying trades within 0.5% of the short strike, or if the uncovered short's |delta| exceeds 0.40.
Close the uncovered short first if spot approaches the short strike - reducing to a 1:1 diagonal restores defined risk.
exit_rules: Close or roll ALL short legs by 14:30 ET on their expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the uncovered short the moment spot touches the short strike; do not wait for a delta or time trigger.
Close any short whose extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close short calls before ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
Buy back the shorts before selling the long.
assignment_risk: Two short contracts, one of them uncovered. Double assignment leaves the account short 200 shares against one long call - a genuinely naked short stock position. This is the structural reason it is level 4 and why the bank marks it as unsuitable for this account.
buying_power: Debit/width treatment on the covered pair plus full naked margin on the uncovered contract (typically $2,000-$8,000).
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 both expiries; the structure must be closeable as a package.
common_mistakes: Selling the second short for a small credit and accepting an unlimited tail; assuming a single long call covers two shorts; leaving the ratio on through an earnings gap.
zero_dte_notes: Never - an uncovered 0DTE short on a share-settled underlying is the worst possible assignment profile.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
